newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals called to open firmer, PGMs up.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals called to open firmer, PGMs up.

text.p: COMEX and NYMEX precious metals futures were called to open firmer Friday, with platinum and palladium soaring higher overnight on continued supply concerns regarding Russian metal, dealers said.

NYMEX July platinum was called to open $12.00 to $22.00 an ounce higher from Thursday's close of $436.60 an ounce, which was $25.00 limit up on the day amid a crisis platinum and palladium dealers meeting in London.
On overnight ACCESS July surged $23.40 higher to $460.00. September palladium was due to open up $6.00 an ounce.
Gold and silver firmed on the white metal rally.
COMEX August gold was called to open $0.50 to $1.00 an ounce higher, while COMEX July silver was due to start trading 9.00 to 10.00 cents firmer.
In London's Friday morning dealings, gold was fixed at $343.80 an ounce, up $3.00 from Thursday afternoon's fixing.
In London platinum was fixed Friday at $495.00, its highest level since August 23, 1990, and palladium established a fresh high at $240.00 an ounce, its best level since March 1980.

Late Thursday following their meeting, London platinum and palladium market markers said there were no defaults in the market and vowed to promote order. The solution lay with Russia renewing supplies, they said.
Meanwhile Friday, financial markets were awaiting the U.S. payroll employment figure for May, forecast at 219,000 new jobs, compared to 142,000 in the previous month.

The payroll employment figure, due at 0830 EDT, also included the unemployment rate for May, forecast at 5.00 percent, up from 4.9 percent in the previous month, along with the hourly earnings and average work week.
Wholesale inventories for April were due at 1000.
COMEX gold stocks Thursday fell 1,061 ounces to 974,833 ounces, while silver stocks fell 351,596 ounces to 202,126,605 ounces.
